newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National bids for Cater Allen.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National bids for Cater Allen.

text.p: British banking group Abbey National Plc said on Thursday that it has made an agreed cash offer for financial services group Cater Allen Holdings Plc, valuing it at 191 million stg.
Abbey National, the fifth largest banking group in the UK, had revealed earlier this month that it was in talks with Cater Allen.

The bank, which already owns 1.1 percent of Cater Allen, is offering 580 pence in cash for each ordinary Cater Allen share, a premium of 31 percent over the closing price of Cater Allen's shares on June 4.
Abbey said that Cater Allen would provide it with a substantial wholesale and retail deposit base together with a new customer base.
"Abbey National's ambitions in these areas would be difficult to achieve organically," said Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch.

Cater Allen, which has its origins as a discount house dealing with the Bank of England, said earlier on Thursday that it made pretax profits of 17.1 million pounds ($28.4 million) for the year to April 30, 1997 compared with 14.6 million previously.
